input.content:
# Launching a Prism Launcher instance and running in-game checks without a human

Research date: 2026-11-07. Nothing was launched and no instance file was changed. Only `--help` and `--version` of the Prism binary were run.

Citation conventions:

- `PRISM:<path>#L<n>` means `https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/blob/11.1.1/<path>#L<n>`, the tag that matches the installed Prism.
- `MC:<path>:<n>` means the decompiled Minecraft 26.1.2 client source, read through the minecraft-modding MCP (Mojang names). Line numbers are those of the decompiled file.
- `NEO:<path>` means `https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/26.1.x/<path>`.
- `$PD` is `~/Library/Application Support/PrismLauncher` (the Prism data dir). `$INST` is `~/prismlauncher/instances` (the instance dir Prism actually uses, see section 2). `$MP` is `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`.

## Recommendation

The short version: a separate test instance, a small dev-only bridge mod that copies Structure Lab's HTTP bridge, and the Prism CLI with `--launch` and `--world`. The owner's ATM11 instance and its "New World" save stay untouched.

1. **Owner decisions first.** These are not filled in here: which world the tests run in (a copy of "New World", the existing 34 MB "Test" world, or a fresh world), the name of the test instance, and whether the agent may create the copy itself. The owner's own notes already say to ask before a jar goes into an instance (`$MP/NOTES.md:359`).
2. **Make a dedicated test instance once.** Copy `$INST/all_the_mods_11_atm11` while the game and Prism are closed. One way is Prism's Copy Instance dialog with the Clone (reflink) option (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceCopyPrefs.h#L27`). The other is `/bin/cp -c -R`, which uses APFS `clonefile` (`/usr/share/man/man1/cp.1:136-140`). Call `/bin/cp` by full path, because in the Bash tool `cp` resolves to GNU coreutils (`man -w cp` gives `/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin/man/man1/cp.1`). Either way the clone shares blocks, so the 23 GB instance costs almost no disk at first (sizes in section 5). The folder name becomes the instance ID used by `--launch` (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceList.cpp#L489`, `PRISM:launcher/BaseInstance.cpp#L276-L278`).
3. **Prepare the copy, not the original.**
   - Replace `minecraft/mods/modular_planters-0.1.0.jar` with the jar from `$MP/build/libs/`.
   - Add the bridge jar (step 4).
   - Set `pauseOnLostFocus:false` in the copy's `options.txt`, or have the bridge set it at runtime the way Structure Lab does (`~/DEV/git_repos/MinecraftStructureInjector/src/main/java/dev/structurelab/LabBridge.java:127`). Otherwise the game pauses as soon as the agent's terminal takes focus (`MC:net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java:1400-1408`). A paused game also pauses the integrated server (`MC:net/minecraft/client/server/IntegratedServer.java:125`), so chunk work and ticking stop and the pause screen covers the HUD.
4. **Build a small dev-only bridge mod**, kept out of the Modular Planters jar the way Structure Lab is (`$MP/build.gradle:126-130`). Copy Structure Lab's transport:
   - an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port and a random bearer token, written to `<gameDir>/<modid>/connection.json` during client setup (`LabBridge.java:43-66`, `LabCapture.java:24`);
   - server-thread work through `server.submit(...)` (`LabBridge.java:68-71`).

   Unlike Structure Lab, it must not freeze ticks or hide the HUD, and it must not be limited to a special world preset (`LabSession.java:41`, `LabSession.java:44-49`, `LabCapture.java:36`). Proposed operations, with the check each one serves:
   - `status`: world loaded, player position, and whether the integrated server is paused. Used by all checks.
   - `command <text>`: run a command as the player through the server command dispatcher, for example `/tp`, `/setblock`, `/place` or `/forceload`. Used by all checks.
   - `aim <x y z>`: teleport the player and set yaw and pitch so the crosshair is on a block. Used for Jade.
   - `jade_tooltip`: return the text of the last tooltip Jade collected. Get it from a Jade `JadeTooltipCollectedCallback` registered through `IWailaClientRegistration.addTooltipCollectedCallback`, reading `BoxElement.getTooltip()` (signatures checked with `javap` against `Jade-mc26.1-NeoForge-26.1.12.jar` in the instance). Because this runs on the physical client after Jade's own provider checks, it shows whether `MPJadePlugin` really contributed lines, which GameTests cannot (`$MP/docs/agents/verifying.md:4`).
   - `guide <entry>`: open the Oracle Index screen on the render thread with `rearth.oracle.OracleClient.openEntry(Identifier, Screen)` or `openScreen(String, Identifier, Screen)` (`~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index/common/src/main/java/rearth/oracle/OracleClient.java:100-134`; both methods are present in the installed `oracle_index-neoforge-2.0.0.jar`, checked with `javap`). Used for Oracle Index.
   - `screenshot`: call `Screenshot.grab(gameDirectory, getMainRenderTarget(), ...)`, the same call F2 makes (`MC:net/minecraft/client/KeyboardHandler.java:476-484`). Leave the HUD and the open screen visible, then read the PNG from `<gameDir>/screenshots/`. Used for Jade and Oracle Index.
   - `chunk_loaded <x z>`: report whether a block position is loaded on the server, using the same `level.isLoaded` test the mod uses (`$MP/src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/multiblock/LiveMultiblock.java:146-148`). NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Unload` can log the exact unload (`NEO:src/main/java/net/neoforged/neoforge/event/level/ChunkEvent.java`, class `Unload` at line 70). Used for the chunk unload check.
   - `quit`: call `Minecraft.getInstance().stop()` on the render thread for a clean, saved shutdown (section 6).
5. **Launch from the agent:**

   ```bash
   "/Applications/Prism Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/prismlauncher" --launch <test-instance-folder> --world "<world folder name>"
   ```

   - `--world` takes the save's folder name, not its display name, because that is what the Worlds page's Join passes (`PRISM:launcher/ui/pages/instance/WorldListPage.cpp#L469-L478`). This matters in "All the Mods 11 - ATM11 (NeoForge Test)", which has two saves shown as "New World", in folders `New World` and `New World (1)` (both `level.dat` files read).
   - Leave out `--offline`. An offline name gives a different player, who would spawn without the owner's inventory (section 1).
   - If Prism's window is already open (it was during this research, PID 7877), the command hands the launch to the running Prism and exits at once (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L453-L497`). Readiness then has to come from the bridge or the log.
6. **Wait for readiness** (section 6):
   - `connection.json` appears in the game dir after client setup;
   - `status` reports a loaded world;
   - `latest.log` shows the join line.
   
   Fail on a new file in `crash-reports/` or on "Game crashed." in the Prism log.
7. **Run the checks through the bridge.**
   - Jade: aim at a formed Planter Core, an unformed one and a growing Planter Block, then read `jade_tooltip` and take a screenshot.
   - Oracle Index: walk the guide entries with `guide`, taking a screenshot of each, and scan `latest.log` for errors.
   - Chunk unload: build a multiblock that crosses a chunk border, teleport the player far away or into another dimension, poll `chunk_loaded` until the far part's chunk is unloaded, wait, return, and confirm the core resumes with nothing lost (the check in `$MP/NOTES.md:359`).
8. **Quit through the bridge**, confirm "Stopping!" in `latest.log` and that the process has exited, and record the results in `NOTES.md`, which is where this project records in-game checks (Entire brain fact `fact:c4362fb921b318616b7c853f`).

Lighter alternative that needs no Prism and no modpack: the repo's dev client already has Jade 26.1.12 and Oracle Index (`$MP/DEVELOPMENT.md:50`, `$MP/NOTES.md:370`). It is a physical client, so the same bridge jar can load through a `-P` switch like `structureLabJar`. A `--quickPlaySingleplayer` program argument would also be needed, and that is a build.gradle change the owner has not approved. For the chunk unload alone, a dev dedicated server (`just server`, `$MP/justfile:59-60`) with `enable-rcon=true` exposes RCON (`MC:net/minecraft/server/dedicated/DedicatedServerProperties.java:84`, `MC:net/minecraft/server/dedicated/DedicatedServer.java:299-302`), and `/forceload add` and `/forceload remove` can load and unload chunks with no client. Neither path tests against the ATM11 mod set.

## 1. Prism Launcher CLI

- **Installed version: 11.1.1.** `CFBundleShortVersionString` in `/Applications/Prism Launcher.app/Contents/Info.plist` is 11.1.1, and `prismlauncher --version` prints `PrismLauncher 11.1.1`. The 11.1.1 release was published 2026-09-28 (`https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/releases/tag/11.1.1`).
- **macOS binary:** `/Applications/Prism Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/prismlauncher` (`CFBundleExecutable` in Info.plist; the file is in that folder). Call it directly. `open -a ... --args` passes arguments only to a newly opened app (`/usr/share/man/man1/open.1:89-92`, `-n` at line 73-74), so it adds nothing over calling the binary.
- **Flags** (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L313-L323`; the same list is printed by `--help` on this machine):
  - `-d/--dir <directory>`: data root;
  - `-l/--launch <instance>`: launch by instance ID;
  - `-s/--server <address>`: join a server;
  - `-w/--world <world>`: join a world;
  - `-a/--profile <profile>`: use the account with this profile name;
  - `-o/--offline <name>`: launch offline with this player name;
  - `--alive`: write `live.check`;
  - `--show-window`: also show the main window;
  - `-I/--import <url>`;
  - `--show <instance>`: open the instance window;
  - `-h`, `--help-all`, `-v`.

  `--server`, `--world`, `--profile` and `--offline` without `--launch` is an error (`#L354-L360`). `--server` wins over `--world` when both are given (`#L1332-L1339`).
- **Instance ID** is the folder name (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceList.cpp#L489`, `PRISM:launcher/BaseInstance.cpp#L276-L278`). The Prism wiki says the same, and its CLI page does not list `--world`, `--offline` or `--show-window` (`https://prismlauncher.org/wiki/getting-started/command-line-interface/`). The source is newer than the wiki.
- **Single-instance hand-off.** Prism changes its working directory to the data dir (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L430`). It then builds an app ID from that path and its version (`#L447`). If a Prism with the same data dir is running, the new process sends it a `launch` message carrying id, world, profile and offline name, then exits (`#L453-L497`). The running Prism handles the message in `messageReceived` (`#L1439-L1476`).
- **What happens after launch.** `performMainStartupAction` turns the world into a `MinecraftTarget` with `useWorld=true` (`#L1336-L1339`; `PRISM:launcher/minecraft/launch/MinecraftTarget.cpp#L21-L27`) and calls `Application::launch` (`#L1349`, body `#L1510-L1551`). Without `--show-window` no main window opens (`#L1351-L1353`).
  - `processMinecraftArgs` adds `--quickPlaySingleplayer <world>` only when the version profile has the trait `feature:is_quick_play_singleplayer` (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp#L758-L769`).
  - The launch script carries `worldName` (`#L813-L819`).
  - The Java side adds `--quickPlaySingleplayer` again from that trait (`PRISM:libraries/launcher/org/prismlauncher/launcher/impl/StandardLauncher.java#L65-L98`).
  - The local Prism metadata for 26.1.2 has that trait. The `+traits` field of `$PD/meta/net.minecraft/26.1.2.json` is `['XR:Initial', 'FirstThreadOnMacOS', 'feature:is_quick_play_singleplayer', 'feature:is_quick_play_multiplayer']`.
- **What "Join" in the Worlds dialog does.** `WorldListPage::on_actionJoin_triggered` calls `APPLICATION->launch(m_inst, LaunchMode::Normal, MinecraftTarget::parse(world->folderName(), true))` (`PRISM:launcher/ui/pages/instance/WorldListPage.cpp#L469-L478`). The button is removed when the instance lacks `feature:is_quick_play_singleplayer` (`#L120-L121`, `#L384-L389`). `--launch X --world Y` follows the same `Application::launch` path, so it does the same thing.
- **Instance setting for auto-join.** `JoinServerOnLaunch`, `JoinServerOnLaunchAddress` and `JoinWorldOnLaunch` (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp#L247-L249`). `JoinWorldOnLaunch` is read only when `JoinServerOnLaunch` is true and the address is empty (`#L1146-L1156`). The CLI flag does not need this setting.
- **Minimum Prism version for world quick play: 9.0.** It came with PR #2716, "Add setting for quickplay singleplayer", merged 2024-08-12 as d2daacf (`https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/pull/2716`). The 9.0 release notes list it (`https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/releases/tag/9.0`, published 2024-10-20). The GitHub compare API reports tag 9.0 as "ahead" of d2daacf and tag 8.4 as "diverged", so 8.4 does not contain it. That PR touched Application.cpp, MinecraftTarget, WorldListPage and StandardLauncher.
- **Accounts.**
  - Without `--profile`, Prism uses the default account. With no default it shows a "No Accounts" box or an account picker, both of which need a human (`PRISM:launcher/LaunchController.cpp#L88-L120`).
  - An account that needs a refresh is refreshed first, and a failed refresh leads to a re-auth prompt or an offline-name dialog (`#L140-L200`, `#L229-L262`).
  - `$PD/accounts.json` exists. It was not read.
  - With `--offline`, the game gets an offline UUID derived from the name when no valid UUID is passed (`MC:net/minecraft/client/main/Main.java:154-156`). Player data is stored per UUID, so this is a different player.

## 3. Vanilla quick play

- Minecraft 26.1.2 accepts:
  - `--quickPlayPath <file>`, required argument;
  - `--quickPlaySingleplayer [world]`, optional argument;
  - `--quickPlayMultiplayer <addr>`;
  - `--quickPlayRealms <id>`.

  Source: `MC:net/minecraft/client/main/Main.java:63-66`.
- `QuickPlay.connect` routes to single player (`MC:net/minecraft/client/quickplay/QuickPlay.java:42-70`).
  - A blank world id means the most recent world (`:55-58`, `getLatestSingleplayerWorld` after line 70).
  - `joinSingleplayerWorld` opens the world if `levelExists(identifier)`. Otherwise it shows an error screen over the world list, and a human or bridge has to handle it (`:87-94`).
  - The identifier is the save folder name.
- `--quickPlayPath` names a JSON file under the game dir (`MC:net/minecraft/client/quickplay/QuickPlayLog.java:38-40`). It is written after the player has logged in to the world (`:50-77`, called from `MC:net/minecraft/client/multiplayer/ClientPacketListener.java:556`), which would make a clean "joined" signal. Prism does not pass `--quickPlayPath`; it adds only `--quickPlaySingleplayer` or `--quickPlayMultiplayer` (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp#L758-L769`). Prism's instance settings expose JVM args and env vars (`#L187-L192`, `#L238-L239`) but no game-argument setting was found.
- How launchers pass it:
  - Prism appends the argument to the game args when the version trait says the version supports it (section 1).
  - Older Minecraft versions without the multiplayer trait get `--server`/`--port` instead (`PRISM:libraries/launcher/org/prismlauncher/launcher/impl/StandardLauncher.java#L84-L98`).
  - Prism also exposes the final arguments as the system property `org.prismlauncher.launch.gameargs` (`#L108-L111`).

The three items are: (J) the Jade tooltips, (O) the Oracle Index book, and (C) a real unload of part of a multiblock's chunks.

## 5. Getting the dev jar into an instance, and the risks

- **Copying `build/libs/*.jar` into `all_the_mods_11_atm11/minecraft/mods`** works technically (section 2), but it puts an unreleased jar into the owner's real game. The next normal play of "New World" (1.5 GB, last written Nov 7 04:00) would load and save Planter Blocks and cores with the dev code. The owner's notes ask for a test world copy and asking first (`$MP/NOTES.md:359`). That instance is also a managed CurseForge pack (`instance.cfg:8-13`), so a pack update could change the mod set under the tests.
- **Recommended: a dedicated copy of the instance.**
  - Sizes: the whole instance is 23 GB. `config` is 8.5 GB, `simplebackups` 7.0 GB, `backups` 3.4 GB, `saves` 1.6 GB and `mods` 856 MB (`du`). The disk has 103 GB free (`df -h`).
  - An APFS clone (`/bin/cp -c -R`, or Prism's Copy Instance with Clone) shares blocks until something is written.
  - Prism's copy dialog can also leave out saves, mods and the rest (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceCopyPrefs.h#L15-L27`).
  - Prism watches the instance dir and finds new folders (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceList.cpp#L79-L82`, `#L470-L489`).
  - Copy while the game is closed, because `session.lock` is held by a running world.
- **Lighter option: a world copy inside the same instance.** Copy only `saves/New World` to a new folder. This protects the save but not the modpack: the dev jar still sits in the owner's real `mods/`, and every world in that instance loads it.
- **The copy's `instance.cfg`** keeps `name=` and `uuid=` from the source (`instance.cfg:27-29`). Two instances would then show the same name in Prism. The ID used by the CLI is still the folder name, so this matters only for the owner's view.

## 6. Detecting launch success or failure, and shutting down cleanly

**Launch detection**

- **Prism's exit code, only when no Prism was running.** Without `--show-window`, Prism opens no window. When the game ends it exits with 0 if the launch succeeded and 1 if it failed (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L1612-L1636`). A non-zero game exit or a crash counts as "Game crashed." (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/launch/LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L172-L196`). One case keeps Prism from exiting: `ShowConsoleOnError=true` (`$PD/prismlauncher.cfg:89`) opens the console window on a crash, and that window stays open until someone closes it (`#L1633` checks for open windows).
- **When Prism is already running**, the CLI exits after handing off the launch (section 1), so its exit code says nothing about the game.
- **The game process** is `java ... org.prismlauncher.EntryPoint` (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/launch/LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L129`). Its working directory is the instance game dir (`#L212-L215`). The access token goes through stdin in the launch script, not the command line (`#L198-L203`, `PRISM:libraries/launcher/org/prismlauncher/EntryPoint.java#L83`, `PRISM:launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp#L872-L876`), so `pgrep -f org.prismlauncher.EntryPoint` is safe to run. Prism logs "Minecraft process ID: <pid>" (`LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L198-L200`).
- **Logs:**
  - Prism writes `$PD/logs/PrismLauncher-0.log` and keeps older ones up to `-4`. Earlier runs logged `Task "LauncherPartLaunch(...)" failed: "Game crashed."` there.
  - The game writes `$INST/<id>/minecraft/logs/latest.log` and `crash-reports/crash-*.txt`.
  - The ready signal is the join line in `latest.log` ("<player> joined the game", from `MinecraftServer` on the server thread), or the bridge's `status` op.
- **Prism `--alive`** writes `live.check` in the data dir once Prism itself has started (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L167`, `#L623-L632`). It says nothing about the game.

**Clean shutdown**

- **Use the bridge's `quit`.** `Minecraft.stop()` sets `running=false` (`MC:net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java:1605-1607`). `Main` then calls `destroy()` in `finally` (`MC:net/minecraft/client/main/Main.java:239-241`). `destroy()` logs "Stopping!", disconnects the level (which saves and stops the integrated server) and calls `System.exit(0)` (`MC:net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java:1185-1214`).
- **Confirm the shutdown** by checking for "Stopping server" and "Stopping!" in `latest.log`, the end of the `EntryPoint` process, and, if Prism was started by the CLI, Prism's exit code 0.
- **Do not use Prism's kill except for a hung game.** `Application::kill` calls `LaunchController::abort` (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L1553-L1568`). Once the game is running, `LauncherPartLaunch::abort` calls `m_process.kill()` (`LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L227-L240`), which skips saving.
- **No in-game stop command:** `/stop` does not exist in single player (`MC:net/minecraft/commands/Commands.java:280-294`).

## Unverified

- **Whether `--world` reaches the world with no screen in between.** Some prompts might appear before the world loads, such as a backup or upgrade prompt or a modded-world warning. Nothing was launched.
- **Whether the default Prism account refreshes without a prompt.** `accounts.json` was not read.
- **Whether the GUI and HUD are drawn into `getMainRenderTarget()` in 26.1.2**, so that `Screenshot.grab` includes Jade's overlay and the Oracle Index screen. The F2 code uses that target, but the render order was not traced.
- **The exact Jade conditions for drawing the overlay** (no screen, HUD on, crosshair hit). These come from Jade's API classes (`RayTracing`, `WailaTickHandler`, `JadeTooltipCollectedCallback` in the installed jar), not from Jade's source. Toggling the two Modular Planters entries in Jade's plugin settings through code was not researched.
- **How long after the player leaves a chunk unloads in 26.1.2**, and whether `/forceload remove` on a dedicated server unloads a chunk with no other ticket (spawn chunks may need the `spawnChunkRadius` gamerule set to 0).
- **Whether a Prism CurseForge pack update removes or keeps a jar added by hand to `mods/`.**
- **Whether the computer-use MCP can grant and drive the Minecraft window**, which shows up as a Java process, and send keys to a GLFW window. It was not tried, because it needs the owner's approval.
- **Whether macOS `screencapture -l` works from the agent's process.** It needs the window ID and Screen Recording permission for the calling app; neither was checked.
- **Whether the absence of a NeoForge client GameTest API is complete.** It rests on a GitHub code search and a file-tree scan of the `26.1.x` branch, which can miss things.
- **Whether `OracleClient.java` in the local clone matches the installed `oracle_index-neoforge-2.0.0.jar` line for line.** Only the method signatures were checked against the jar.
- **The Structure Lab working tree, which has uncommitted changes** (`git status`: `LabBridge.java`, `LabCapture.java` and `neoforge.mods.toml` modified). The citations to it are to the working tree, not to a commit.

# Launching a Prism Launcher instance and running in-game checks without a human

Research date: 2026-11-07. Nothing was launched and no instance file was changed. Only `--help` and `--version` of the Prism binary were run.

Citation conventions:

- `PRISM:<path>#L<n>` means `https://github.com/PrismLauncher/PrismLauncher/blob/11.1.1/<path>#L<n>`, the tag that matches the installed Prism.
- `MC:<path>:<n>` means the decompiled Minecraft 26.1.2 client source, read through the minecraft-modding MCP (Mojang names). Line numbers are those of the decompiled file.
- `NEO:<path>` means `https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/26.1.x/<path>`.
- `$PD` is `~/Library/Application Support/PrismLauncher` (the Prism data dir). `$INST` is `~/prismlauncher/instances` (the instance dir Prism actually uses, see section 2). `$MP` is `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`.

## Recommendation

The short version: a separate test instance, a small dev-only bridge mod that copies Structure Lab's HTTP bridge, and the Prism CLI with `--launch` and `--world`. The owner's ATM11 instance and its "New World" save stay untouched.

1. **Owner decisions first.** These are not filled in here: which world the tests run in (a copy of "New World", the existing 34 MB "Test" world, or a fresh world), the name of the test instance, and whether the agent may create the copy itself. The owner's own notes already say to ask before a jar goes into an instance (`$MP/NOTES.md:359`).
2. **Make a dedicated test instance once.** Copy `$INST/all_the_mods_11_atm11` while the game and Prism are closed. One way is Prism's Copy Instance dialog with the Clone (reflink) option (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceCopyPrefs.h#L27`). The other is `/bin/cp -c -R`, which uses APFS `clonefile` (`/usr/share/man/man1/cp.1:136-140`). Call `/bin/cp` by full path, because in the Bash tool `cp` resolves to GNU coreutils (`man -w cp` gives `/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin/man/man1/cp.1`). Either way the clone shares blocks, so the 23 GB instance costs almost no disk at first (sizes in section 5). The folder name becomes the instance ID used by `--launch` (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceList.cpp#L489`, `PRISM:launcher/BaseInstance.cpp#L276-L278`).
3. **Prepare the copy, not the original.**
   - Replace `minecraft/mods/modular_planters-0.1.0.jar` with the jar from `$MP/build/libs/`.
   - Add the bridge jar (step 4).
   - Set `pauseOnLostFocus:false` in the copy's `options.txt`, or have the bridge set it at runtime the way Structure Lab does (`~/DEV/git_repos/MinecraftStructureInjector/src/main/java/dev/structurelab/LabBridge.java:127`). Otherwise the game pauses as soon as the agent's terminal takes focus (`MC:net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java:1400-1408`). A paused game also pauses the integrated server (`MC:net/minecraft/client/server/IntegratedServer.java:125`), so chunk work and ticking stop and the pause screen covers the HUD.
4. **Build a small dev-only bridge mod**, kept out of the Modular Planters jar the way Structure Lab is (`$MP/build.gradle:126-130`). Copy Structure Lab's transport:
   - an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port and a random bearer token, written to `<gameDir>/<modid>/connection.json` during client setup (`LabBridge.java:43-66`, `LabCapture.java:24`);
   - server-thread work through `server.submit(...)` (`LabBridge.java:68-71`).

   Unlike Structure Lab, it must not freeze ticks or hide the HUD, and it must not be limited to a special world preset (`LabSession.java:41`, `LabSession.java:44-49`, `LabCapture.java:36`). Proposed operations, with the check each one serves:
   - `status`: world loaded, player position, and whether the integrated server is paused. Used by all checks.
   - `command <text>`: run a command as the player through the server command dispatcher, for example `/tp`, `/setblock`, `/place` or `/forceload`. Used by all checks.
   - `aim <x y z>`: teleport the player and set yaw and pitch so the crosshair is on a block. Used for Jade.
   - `jade_tooltip`: return the text of the last tooltip Jade collected. Get it from a Jade `JadeTooltipCollectedCallback` registered through `IWailaClientRegistration.addTooltipCollectedCallback`, reading `BoxElement.getTooltip()` (signatures checked with `javap` against `Jade-mc26.1-NeoForge-26.1.12.jar` in the instance). Because this runs on the physical client after Jade's own provider checks, it shows whether `MPJadePlugin` really contributed lines, which GameTests cannot (`$MP/docs/agents/verifying.md:4`).
   - `guide <entry>`: open the Oracle Index screen on the render thread with `rearth.oracle.OracleClient.openEntry(Identifier, Screen)` or `openScreen(String, Identifier, Screen)` (`~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/oracle-index/common/src/main/java/rearth/oracle/OracleClient.java:100-134`; both methods are present in the installed `oracle_index-neoforge-2.0.0.jar`, checked with `javap`). Used for Oracle Index.
   - `screenshot`: call `Screenshot.grab(gameDirectory, getMainRenderTarget(), ...)`, the same call F2 makes (`MC:net/minecraft/client/KeyboardHandler.java:476-484`). Leave the HUD and the open screen visible, then read the PNG from `<gameDir>/screenshots/`. Used for Jade and Oracle Index.
   - `chunk_loaded <x z>`: report whether a block position is loaded on the server, using the same `level.isLoaded` test the mod uses (`$MP/src/main/java/io/github/julianperge/modular_planters/multiblock/LiveMultiblock.java:146-148`). NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Unload` can log the exact unload (`NEO:src/main/java/net/neoforged/neoforge/event/level/ChunkEvent.java`, class `Unload` at line 70). Used for the chunk unload check.

It freezes ticks only in its own preset world (`LabSession.java:29`, `:41`) | No (HUD hidden) | No (screens closed) | Partly: `inspect` can read block states, but it has no command or teleport op |

- **Copying `build/libs/*.jar` into `all_the_mods_11_atm11/minecraft/mods`** works technically (section 2), but it puts an unreleased jar into the owner's real game. The next normal play of "New World" (1.5 GB, last written Nov 7 04:00) would load and save Planter Blocks and cores with the dev code. The owner's notes ask for a test world copy and asking first (`$MP/NOTES.md:359`). That instance is also a managed CurseForge pack (`instance.cfg:8-13`), so a pack update could change the mod set under the tests.
- **Recommended: a dedicated copy of the instance.**
  - Sizes: the whole instance is 23 GB. `config` is 8.5 GB, `simplebackups` 7.0 GB, `backups` 3.4 GB, `saves` 1.6 GB and `mods` 856 MB (`du`). The disk has 103 GB free (`df -h`).
  - An APFS clone (`/bin/cp -c -R`, or Prism's Copy Instance with Clone) shares blocks until something is written.
  - Prism's copy dialog can also leave out saves, mods and the rest (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceCopyPrefs.h#L15-L27`).
  - Prism watches the instance dir and finds new folders (`PRISM:launcher/InstanceList.cpp#L79-L82`, `#L470-L489`).
  - Copy while the game is closed, because `session.lock` is held by a running world.
- **Lighter option: a world copy inside the same instance.** Copy only `saves/New World` to a new folder. This protects the save but not the modpack: the dev jar still sits in the owner's real `mods/`, and every world in that instance loads it.
- **The copy's `instance.cfg`** keeps `name=` and `uuid=` from the source (`instance.cfg:27-29`). Two instances would then show the same name in Prism. The ID used by the CLI is still the folder name, so this matters only for the owner's view.

## 6. Detecting launch success or failure, and shutting down cleanly

**Launch detection**

- **Prism's exit code, only when no Prism was running.** Without `--show-window`, Prism opens no window. When the game ends it exits with 0 if the launch succeeded and 1 if it failed (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L1612-L1636`). A non-zero game exit or a crash counts as "Game crashed." (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/launch/LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L172-L196`). One case keeps Prism from exiting: `ShowConsoleOnError=true` (`$PD/prismlauncher.cfg:89`) opens the console window on a crash, and that window stays open until someone closes it (`#L1633` checks for open windows).
- **When Prism is already running**, the CLI exits after handing off the launch (section 1), so its exit code says nothing about the game.
- **The game process** is `java ... org.prismlauncher.EntryPoint` (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/launch/LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L129`). Its working directory is the instance game dir (`#L212-L215`). The access token goes through stdin in the launch script, not the command line (`#L198-L203`, `PRISM:libraries/launcher/org/prismlauncher/EntryPoint.java#L83`, `PRISM:launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp#L872-L876`), so `pgrep -f org.prismlauncher.EntryPoint` is safe to run. Prism logs "Minecraft process ID: <pid>" (`LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L198-L200`).
- **Logs:**
  - Prism writes `$PD/logs/PrismLauncher-0.log` and keeps older ones up to `-4`. Earlier runs logged `Task "LauncherPartLaunch(...)" failed: "Game crashed."` there.
  - The game writes `$INST/<id>/minecraft/logs/latest.log` and `crash-reports/crash-*.txt`.
  - The ready signal is the join line in `latest.log` ("<player> joined the game", from `MinecraftServer` on the server thread), or the bridge's `status` op.
- **Prism `--alive`** writes `live.check` in the data dir once Prism itself has started (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L167`, `#L623-L632`). It says nothing about the game.

**Clean shutdown**

- **Use the bridge's `quit`.** `Minecraft.stop()` sets `running=false` (`MC:net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java:1605-1607`). `Main` then calls `destroy()` in `finally` (`MC:net/minecraft/client/main/Main.java:239-241`). `destroy()` logs "Stopping!", disconnects the level (which saves and stops the integrated server) and calls `System.exit(0)` (`MC:net/minecraft/client/Minecraft.java:1185-1214`).
- **Confirm the shutdown** by checking for "Stopping server" and "Stopping!" in `latest.log`, the end of the `EntryPoint` process, and, if Prism was started by the CLI, Prism's exit code 0.
- **Do not use Prism's kill except for a hung game.** `Application::kill` calls `LaunchController::abort` (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L1553-L1568`). Once the game is running, `LauncherPartLaunch::abort` calls `m_process.kill()` (`LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L227-L240`), which skips saving.
- **No in-game stop command:** `/stop` does not exist in single player (`MC:net/minecraft/commands/Commands.java:280-294`).

## Unverified

- **Whether `--world` reaches the world with no screen in between.** Some prompts might appear before the world loads, such as a backup or upgrade prompt or a modded-world warning. Nothing was launched.
- **Whether the default Prism account refreshes without a prompt.** `accounts.json` was not read.

- **Whether a Prism CurseForge pack update removes or keeps a jar added by hand to `mods/`.**
- **Whether the computer-use MCP can grant and drive the Minecraft window**, which shows up as a Java process, and send keys to a GLFW window. It was not tried, because it needs the owner's approval.
- **Whether macOS `screencapture -l` works from the agent's process.** It needs the window ID and Screen Recording permission for the calling app; neither was checked.
- **Whether the absence of a NeoForge client GameTest API is complete.** It rests on a GitHub code search and a file-tree scan of the `26.1.x` branch, which can miss things.
- **Whether `OracleClient.java` in the local clone matches the installed `oracle_index-neoforge-2.0.0.jar` line for line.** Only the method signatures were checked against the jar.

content.content:
77:- **Single-instance hand-off.** Prism changes its working directory to the data dir (`PRISM:launcher/Application.cpp#L430`). It then builds an app ID from that path and its version (`#L447`). If a Prism with the same data dir is running, the new process sends it a `launch` message carrying id, world, profile and offline name, then exits (`#L453-L497`). The running Prism handles the message in `messageReceived` (`#L1439-L1476`).
90:  - With `--offline`, the game gets an offline UUID derived from the name when no valid UUID is passed (`MC:net/minecraft/client/main/Main.java:154-156`). Player data is stored per UUID, so this is a different player.
145:| Server commands typed by a human-like driver | `/tp`, `/forceload`, `/setblock` and `/place` need cheats. Both ATM11 saves checked have `allowCommands` 1 (`level.dat`). `/stop` and `/save-all` exist only on a dedicated server (`MC:net/minecraft/commands/Commands.java:280-294`) | Setup only | Setup only | Yes, with something to send the commands |
177:- **The game process** is `java ... org.prismlauncher.EntryPoint` (`PRISM:launcher/minecraft/launch/LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L129`). Its working directory is the instance game dir (`#L212-L215`). The access token goes through stdin in the launch script, not the command line (`#L198-L203`, `PRISM:libraries/launcher/org/prismlauncher/EntryPoint.java#L83`, `PRISM:launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp#L872-L876`), so `pgrep -f org.prismlauncher.EntryPoint` is safe to run. Prism logs "Minecraft process ID: <pid>" (`LauncherPartLaunch.cpp#L198-L200`).
189:- **No in-game stop command:** `/stop` does not exist in single player (`MC:net/minecraft/commands/Commands.java:280-294`).

The full report is at /Users/sweetjp/tmp/2026-11-07-prism-launch-research/prism-launch-research.md. Nothing was launched and no instance files were changed.

**Recommendation:**
- Clone `all_the_mods_11_atm11` into a separate test instance, using APFS clone with `/bin/cp -c -R` or Prism's Copy Instance with Clone. Put the dev jar in the clone.
- Add a small dev-only bridge mod built like Structure Lab's localhost HTTP bridge. Its ops are status, command, aim, jade_tooltip (through Jade's `JadeTooltipCollectedCallback`), guide (`OracleClient.openEntry`), screenshot, chunk_loaded and quit.
- Launch with `"/Applications/Prism Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/prismlauncher" --launch <folder-id> --world "<save folder>"`. This does the same as the Worlds dialog's "Join". Installed Prism is 11.1.1; world quick play needs Prism 9.0 or later.
- Set pauseOnLostFocus to false, or the game pauses when the agent's terminal has focus. Shut down with `Minecraft.stop()`, not Prism's kill, which skips saving.

**Key findings:**
- Prism uses `~/prismlauncher/instances`. The instances under Application Support are stale.
- ATM11 runs NeoForge 26.1.2.126, which meets the mod's `[26.1.2.116,)` range. Modular Planters 0.1.0 is already loaded there from an Oct 31 jar.
- The NeoForge Test instance (26.1.2.106) cannot load the mod.
- If Prism is already open, the CLI hands the launch to it and exits at once. Readiness then has to come from the bridge or `latest.log`.
- Single player has no RCON.
- Open questions for the owner: which world to test in, the test instance's name, and whether the agent may make the copy.
